commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

`server/mcp/tool-executor.ts` now typechecks clean.

**Verification** — `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`:
- target file: **29 errors → 0**
- other files: I diffed the full compiler output before vs. after (baseline taken by restoring `HEAD:server/mcp/tool-executor.ts`, then restoring my version). The diff contains **only deletions** — the removed lines are continuation detail of the target file's own errors. No new error appears anywhere.
- No `@ts-ignore`/`@ts-expect-error`/`@ts-nocheck`, no `any` casts added, no code deleted to dodge a check.

**What the fixes were**, grouped by root cause:

1. **Untyped JSON-RPC args (`unknown`) flowing into typed calls** — the bulk of the errors (`args?.x || 'default'` widens to `{}`). Added small narrowing helpers at the trust boundary the file already documents: `asString`, `asOptionalString`, `asNumber`, `asRecord`, `asStringArray`. Applied to `generateArtifact`, `runEscalation`, `checkContentEnforcement`, `governedGenerate`, and the narrative/digestibility handlers. The redundant `typeof x === 'string' ? x : String(x)` dance in `governedGenerate` is gone now that the values are typed strings.
2. **`Surface` union (line 250)** — added `asSurface`, which matches the argument against the gate's nine surfaces via `find`, defaulting to `'general'`. Type-only import of `Surface`, so the deliberate dynamic `import('./fail-closed-gate')` stays dynamic.
3. **`json(...)` — an undefined function** in all 11 `surfaceGovernance.*` handlers. It was `mcpText` under another name (same signature, same return type); these handlers would have thrown `ReferenceError` at runtime. Now `mcpText`.
4. **`SurfaceFinding.file`** doesn't exist. Sourced from `f.patch?.file ?? f.location` so the output key stays `file` for consumers.
5. **Control-plane gate** — `surface`/`riskScore` aren't in `EnforceRequest` (they belong to `EnforcementRequest` in `enforcement-layer.ts`); moved into `metadata`, which `recordAudit` preserves into the ledger, so the data still reaches the audit row. `cpResult.blocked` → `!cpResult.allowed`, the field `EnforceResult` actually has.
6. **`ctx.userId`** — added as a documented optional field on `ExecutionContext`. No caller supplies it today, so the `'mcp-caller'` fallback behavior is unchanged; the alternative (deriving `agentId` from `authenticatedTenant`) would have changed which agent policy applies to authenticated tenants, which is a governance behavior change this task shouldn't make.

One behavior note worth flagging: in `auditNarrativeCoherence`, `args.routes` is now filtered to a genuine `string[]` before reaching `auditWebsiteRoutes` — a mixed-type array that previously slipped through now falls back to the full-site audit rather than passing non-strings into a `string[]` parameter.
